posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
On my current table, I've got the laser mounted using a wooden clothespin glued to the jig. One of my concerns is with the stiffness of the wire that I've got going between the driver and the diode, maybe it should be replaced with much more flexible wire (it's stranded, but not very fine). How do you mount your laser?

I have some web documents on holography which I've created - they're at

[http://members.shaw.ca/ted.park/holograms.html](http://members.shaw.ca/ted.park/holograms.html)

--Ted

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: I have destroyed diodes by using too stiff wire. Bumping into them in the dark tends to break the very fine wires in the inside. My solutiotion was to get some 23 guage stranded 3 conductor wire. The type I got was teflon coated and sold by Mc Master Carr. We use it at B3 for thermostat wires that get close to the flame.

posts.author: tpark
posts.content_md:
I have the wires soldered to a socket, and the diode/lens assembly is pushed into that. It sounds like it might be a good idea to get some better wire though. I'll try the fine teflon wire.

--Ted
